mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong earnings growth (INDPRO > 0.5% monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above trend within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months indicates persistent labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate margin potential, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or payroll growth (PAYEMS) accelerates sharply in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 0.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in INDPRO is reversed in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months signals weakness in the housing sector, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1.2 million for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or HOUST rebounds above 1.3 million in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month, combined with a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressure and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a late-cycle expansion regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows positive acceleration and UNRATE falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes during a late-cycle expansion, or unemployment rises in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue prospects for consumer-facing sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or RSAFS rebounds above its moving average within two months.
